ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The figure shows a map with some islands and how they are connected by bridges. A navigator wants to pass through each of the islands exactly once. He started at Cang Island and wants to finish at Uru Island. He has just arrived at the black island in the center of the map. In which direction must he go now to be able to complete his route?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the image, the purple island in the upper left is labeled Cang, and the orange island in the lower right is labeled Uru. The central black island has bridges in four directions: north to the cyan island above, south to the cyan island below, west to the cyan island on the left, and east to the cyan island on the right. The compass shows that up is north, down is south, left is west, and right is east. Reasoning: Treat the islands as vertices and the bridges as edges. The route must go from Cang to Uru and pass through each island exactly once, so except for Cang and Uru, each intermediate island must have two used bridges in the final route, while Cang and Uru each have only one. Starting from the many islands in the image that have only two bridges, forced inference: Cang cannot go downward, otherwise the top-row island to its right would be cut off; therefore the route advances rightward from Cang along the top row. The top row and the right-side chain continue to be forced, making the route enter the black island after passing through the island north of the central black island, that is, the north-side bridge of the black island is already the entry bridge. The lower-left chain is also forced: a string of islands on the left side and bottom with degree 2 must connect into a segment, which makes the adjacent island on the west side of the black island already need to connect to the lower-left chain and unable to connect to the black island again, so the black island cannot go west. If the black island goes east, then the black island, the island to its north, the adjacent island on the northeast side, and the island to the east would form a small closed loop, closing before reaching Uru, and the full route from Cang to Uru cannot be completed. Therefore the black island also cannot go east. The black island has already been entered from the north, and west and east are both infeasible, so the only exit that can continue to complete the route is south.

method.method_draft: Read the islands as vertices and bridges as graph edges. From the image, label the purple top-left island as Cang, the orange bottom-right island as Uru, and the black central island as the current vertex. Use the fact that every island other than Cang and Uru must have exactly two used bridges in the final route, while Cang and Uru have exactly one. Then force all degree-2 islands: the top-left route from Cang must go through the upper chain toward the right/top side; the left-lower chain forces the bridge from the black island downward to be used, while choosing the west/east alternatives would either strand an island or create a closed loop before reaching Uru. Continuing the forced-edge propagation gives the route segment approaching the black island from the north and leaving it to the south. Therefore the required next direction is South.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中左上角紫色岛标为 Cang，右下角橙色岛标为 Uru。中央黑色岛有四个方向的桥：向北连到上方青色岛，向南连到下方青色岛，向西连到左侧青色岛，向东连到右侧青色岛。指南针显示上方为北、下方为南、左方为西、右方为东。

推理：把岛看作顶点、桥看作边。路线要从 Cang 到 Uru 且每个岛正好经过一次，所以除 Cang 和 Uru 外，每个中间岛在最终路线中都必须有两条被使用的桥，Cang 和 Uru 各只有一条。

从图中许多只有两条桥的岛开始强制推断：Cang 不能向下走，否则它右边的顶排岛会被断开；因此路线从 Cang 沿顶排向右推进。顶排和右侧链继续强制，使路线经过中央黑岛北边的岛后进入黑岛，也就是黑岛的北侧桥已经是进入桥。

左下方的链也被强制：左侧和底部的一串度数为 2 的岛必须连成一段，这会使黑岛西侧相邻岛已经需要连接到左下链，不能再接黑岛，所以黑岛不能向西走。

若黑岛向东走，则黑岛、其北边岛、东北侧相邻岛、东边岛会形成一个小闭环，尚未到达 Uru 就封闭，不能完成从 Cang 到 Uru 的全路线。因此黑岛也不能向东走。

黑岛已经从北边进入，西、东都不可行，所以唯一能继续完成路线的出口是向南。

method.method_draft: Convert the pictured map into an adjacency list, then perform a systematic Hamiltonian-path search from Cang to Uru. Treat each possible bridge out of the black island—north, south, east, and west—as a candidate successor after the black island. For each candidate, run backtracking or exact-cover search requiring every island to be visited once and ending at Uru. The branches where the black island is followed by north, east, or west fail because the remaining graph cannot be completed into a single Hamiltonian path ending at Uru. The only branch that admits a complete path has the black island followed by its southern neighbor. Hence the navigator must go South.

raw_record.final_cot:

The central black island has bridges in four directions: north to the cyan island above, south to the cyan island below, west to the cyan island on the left, and east to the cyan island on the right. The compass shows that up is north, down is south, left is west, and right is east.

Reasoning: Treat the islands as vertices and the bridges as edges. The route must go from Cang to Uru and pass through each island exactly once, so except for Cang and Uru, each intermediate island must have two used bridges in the final route, while Cang and Uru each have only one.

Starting from the many islands in the image that have only two bridges, forced inference: Cang cannot go downward, otherwise the top-row island to its right would be cut off; therefore the route advances rightward from Cang along the top row. The top row and the right-side chain continue to be forced, making the route enter the black island after passing through the island north of the central black island, that is, the north-side bridge of the black island is already the entry bridge.

The lower-left chain is also forced: a string of islands on the left side and bottom with degree 2 must connect into a segment, which makes the adjacent island on the west side of the black island already need to connect to the lower-left chain and unable to connect to the black island again, so the black island cannot go west.

If the black island goes east, then the black island, the island to its north, the adjacent island on the northeast side, and the island to the east would form a small closed loop, closing before reaching Uru, and the full route from Cang to Uru cannot be completed. Therefore the black island also cannot go east.

The black island has already been entered from the north, and west and east are both infeasible, so the only exit that can continue to complete the route is south.
